On a rainy, cold day in early February, I visited the tiny village of Al-Jib. A group of Israeli activists had gathered to hear from residents about the devastating effects of the wall and settlements on their lives. As we drove into the town, the road narrowed and became very bumpy. We were now driving over gravel roads that led up into the hills surrounding Al-Jib. The landscape was breathtaking: lush green trees with deep red fruit hanging down and golden flowers sprouting everywhere. Houses were built on top of hills, with terracotta roofs that matched the red soil below them. The views were expansive—looking out towards the Jordan Valley in one direction, and the West Bank and Jerusalem in the other.

Winning a Nobel Prize could hurt your career. That's the conclusion of research by economists Matthew Gentzkow, Jesse Shapiro and Matthew Weinzierl, who found that winners' scientific impact slowed after they were honored with the world's most prestigious award in science. The authors studied 135 American and British scientists who won the prize between 1901 and 2008. They looked at citations to their work from other papers published before and after the awards -- a measure of how often others cite them. The word phonics comes from Greek, and it means "sounds." This is a method that teaches children to associate sounds with letters. Children learn to recognize and write the letters in words as well as how to pronounce them correctly. Phonics can be taught using different methods. One way is through pictures. Teachers show students pictures of items that begin with specific sounds. Another way is through stories. Students are shown pictures of items that begin with certain sounds. When they see these items in the story, they say the sounds. The teacher may also help them learn how to spell these words by sounding out each letter.

In other words, if you are a student with perfect attendance, you would get an A, even if you never did your homework or took a single test all semester. ACROSTIC — Today’s poem is an acrostic. This form has several advantages, which I will explain as we go along. First, the reader can easily see all of the letters used in each line. Second, it gives the poet a chance to use interesting words. Third, it gives the poet a chance to tell about one subject with many different points of view and from multiple perspectives. For example, a trip to the zoo could be described from the perspective of the animals, the children who visit, or the parents. Fourth, it allows you to write about your favorite things in alphabetical order. Finally, acrostics are fun to write!

The word plaudit, as in “plaudits,” comes from Latin and means a cry or applause. The English noun plauditor is a person who gives plaudits. ACROSTIC — Today’s word is a form of poetry in which the first letters, when read downward and across from left to right, spell out a particular message. This form of poetry was developed by a French poet named Charles d’Orléans (1394-1465). The word acrostic comes from Greek and means “the same at both ends.” A person who writes an acrostic poem creates a series of lines that are arranged so that each line starts with a letter of the alphabet. Once you have arranged the words or phrases into your poem, it will be necessary to arrange them so that they form an acrostic. The first letter in each line spells something specific—a name, a place, a message, a secret code

Why do you need to tip at all? It's a way of paying for service with money. That is, it is a form of compensation for labor and that is what makes it a payment (even if in an indirect way). ACROSTIC — There is a line in the poem that gives the title. The first letter of each word in the line spells out a word or phrase related to the poem’s topic. For example, if the line is “Bright sunshine and warm winds,” the acrostic would be “sun” “shine” “warm” “wind.” It could also be written backwards, as in “I was a dreamer before I was awake” for the following acrostic: “dreamer” “before” “awake” “was.” A simple form of acrostics uses only one letter per line; an extended form uses two letters per line.

The word globalization comes from the Latin globus, meaning a round object. The term was first used in 1930 to describe the expansion of industrial production and trade throughout the world. In the late 20th century, however, it came to mean the integration of economies and societies around the world through international organizations like the World Trade Organization (WTO) and the World Bank. By the beginning of the 21st century, the term had expanded to include the spread of information technology and the development of multinational corporations. Globalization is often seen as a phenomenon with both positive and negative effects on societies and cultures around the world.

One hundred and fifty years ago, the first settlers arrived on the Great Plains. The region had long been inhabited by Native Americans who had managed its ecosystems for centuries with great care. But these new arrivals brought a host of novel forces that would transform the landscape forever: railroads, barbed wire, the plow. The result was an environmental catastrophe. Forests were cut down to make way for farms; grasslands were plowed under in favor of crops. The prairie’s biodiversity plummeted, along with water tables and soil fertility. George Kennan lost his faith in the possibility of an American-style democratic future for Russia, a conviction he had shared with many other Americans. He became convinced that Russia would remain a backward and untrustworthy society whose only salvation lay in the hands of the communist party. The Russian people were doomed to be "ruled by tyrants until they are crushed or driven out of existence." The hope of a better life for Russians, Kennan concluded, was "unattainable through any human agency," least of all one based on democracy. Kennan's dark assessment of Russia's future, while not new, gained greater weight when it came from someone so influential as Kennan.

In “Primavera,” Louise Glück writes about the cycle of life, but also how we as humans are not always in control of our lives. She uses the symbol of a tree to portray the idea that sometimes we have to go through something tough before we can grow into who we want to be. In the poem she talks about a girl and her father who are planting a tree, and while they’re working on it, the girl thinks about all of the things that she wants out of life. But as soon as the girl begins thinking about all of these things, the tree dies and falls over. The narrator then explains that when the girl is older, she will learn that no matter how much she thinks about what she wants in life, it might just not happen for her.

Sometimes social revolutions are triggered by a single individual who articulates an idea that resonates with the people. Sometimes they happen because of a group of individuals whose ideas and actions create a movement. Occasionally, it takes a person in the right place at the right time to be the spark that ignites the fire. But more often than not, revolutionary movements begin slowly. They start with a few people who share common concerns, but who have yet to come together as a cohesive force. Those early adopters are usually isolated from one another and lack resources to make their vision reality. It's only when those people find each other and develop strategies for bringing about change that real progress begins. The first step is always building trust among people who might otherwise never interact or even meet.

CRYPTIC CROSSWORD — A cryptic crossword is a type of word puzzle in which the answers are phrases or sentences, rather than words. The clues to these puzzles are written using double definitions. The two parts of each clue refer to different aspects of the answer and are typically interwoven into a single sentence. For example, a clue might read "Chair that's very hard (5)" and the answer would be "STONE". Clue 1 would then be "Chair", and Clue 2 would be "very hard". In this case, the answer is "stone". The two parts of the clue are joined together by a pun on the word "stone".

The word kowtow is a verb that means to show respect or subservience by bowing down, especially in a formal manner. It comes from the Chinese kuo2 tou1, which was originally an expression used to describe how Chinese people would bow down to their superiors during imperial times. In modern usage, it refers to any gesture of humility and submission. The word entered English around 1700.

The word klaxon is an English word that means "a sound used to warn or signal someone". It was first recorded in 1865-70, and its origin is unknown. It may be related to the Greek verb galaō, meaning 'to shout'. It may also be a back-formation from the surname Klaasen. The word is often used figuratively for something that warns, such as the warning bell on a bicycle. It has been suggested that it may be derived from the Dutch name for a horn (klok), but this explanation has been rejected by the Oxford English Dictionary.
